resolvedIssues.title: npm run coverage intermittently exits 1 on a stray post-teardown React setState in a QA test, under v8 coverage instrumentation only
resolvedIssues.expected: npm run coverage should exit 0 deterministically, per this self-test assignment's check suite and the developer-loop skill's Test step.
resolvedIssues.actual: npm run coverage (root chain: server then client) exited 1 on 1 of 3 runs this session with a Vitest 'Unhandled Rejection: ReferenceError: window is not defined' at LoginPage.jsx:62 (the handleSubmit finally block's setSubmitting(false)), caught after the jsdom test environment for client/tests/qa/qa-login-register.test.jsx had already torn down. All 236 server + 165 client tests still reported as passed in every run, including the failing one; only the trailing unhandled-rejection line flipped the process exit code. Isolated npm run coverage -w client reruns: 3 of 4 exited 0, 1 of 4 exited 1 with the identical stack (confirmed identical via grep across the two failing logs). Plain npm test -w client (no coverage) never reproduced it in 1 run this session.
resolvedIssues.reproduction: From the repo root or client/, run `npm run coverage` (or `npm run coverage -w client`) 3-5 times in a row; before the repair, roughly 1 in 3-4 runs exited 1 with the exact stack trace in evidence/selftest/coverage-flake.md.
resolvedIssues.suggestedFix: Guard the post-await setSubmitting/setFieldErrors/setFormError calls in LoginPage.jsx's handleSubmit (and the equivalent in RegisterPage.jsx) with an unmounted-ref or AbortController check so a late-resolving mock cannot call setState after unmount; or have QA's test await the mocked response settling before the test ends. Not fixed by developer in this test-only phase (no product code changes permitted; also a QA-owned test file). Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to any of the 15 D-DES fixes: git diff de83b87 ec7323f -- client/src/pages/LoginPage.jsx shows only the additive D-DES-001 Mail-icon import/prop; handleSubmit (including the exact reported line) is byte-identical to iteration 1.
resolvedIssues.owningArea: tooling/build (test-infrastructure timing; the touched product line itself is unchanged from iteration 1)
resolvedIssues.resolution: Resolved by QA in cycle-01 (.workflow/sprints/delivery/iteration-02/qa/cycle-01/), NOT by developer. QA added additive await-sequencing (no assertion changes) to client/tests/qa/qa-login-register.test.jsx in two places: QA-CC-04 ('a slow login submits exactly once on a rapid double click') and a second identical race in QA-CC-08 ('the submit button shows a pending/disabled state while the login is in flight') — both now wait for the post-login budget fetch (or an equivalent settle point) before the test ends, so the mocked login promise (and LoginPage.jsx's handleSubmit finally block) has fully resolved while the jsdom environment is still alive, leaving nothing pending at teardown. Developer independently verified this session: (1) read-only inspection of the git diff for qa-login-register.test.jsx confirmed the change is exactly the additive waitFor sequencing described, no assertion changes; (2) QA's own cycle-01 evidence shows 6/6 consecutive npm run coverage runs exit 0 (.workflow/sprints/delivery/iteration-02/qa/cycle-01/evidence/coverage-run-1.log through -6.log); (3) developer independently re-ran npm run coverage 3 more consecutive times from the repo root afterward — all 3 exit 0 (236 server + 165 client tests each, zero unhandled rejections). Developer did not modify qa/ or any product file to effect this resolution.
